playbooks.title: General capture health

checks.description: Use health and Expert counts to choose the next aggregate query

successPath: Read the overview first
Query aggregate evidence before packet detail
Use packet summaries and fields only to locate evidence

failureBranches.condition: A source is truncated or a query fails
failureBranches.limitation: State the incomplete coverage and do not infer an absence.

requiredLimitations: Conclusions require tool evidence.
Truncated or failed sources limit negative conclusions.

playbooks.title: IMS registration failure

checks.description: Read the SIP registrationAnalyses projection to locate the initial REGISTER, challenge, authenticated retry, final response, selected attempt, and alternate candidates
Check the same registration window for TCP retransmission, RST, Zero Window, ICMP, and Expert evidence

successPath: Call get_capture_overview first
Call get_communication_analysis with domains=[sip] and protocol=register
Confirm a final 2xx REGISTER response
Report the correlated request, challenge, authenticated retry, and response frames
Use get_statistics for the selected time window when transport evidence is needed

failureBranches.condition: SIP is absent or protected by IPsec
failureBranches.limitation: State that SIP registration signaling is not visible; do not infer registration success or failure.

failureBranches.condition: The SIP source is truncated or no final response is visible
failureBranches.limitation: State the observed signaling gap and coverage limit; call it a timeout only when the local projection reports complete negative evidence.

requiredLimitations: Authorization values are never available; only presence and scheme may be used.
A missing encrypted or truncated signaling path limits negative conclusions.
Network response codes describe observed signaling, not an absolute operator-specific root cause.

playbooks.title: IMS call setup failure

checks.description: Read callSetupAnalysis to select exactly one INVITE and cite each derived stage boundary, final response, ACK state, and alternate candidates
Inspect the response frame and only transport evidence already correlated by call time window and endpoints

successPath: Call get_capture_overview first
Call get_communication_analysis with domains=[sip]
Use callSetupAnalysis rather than mixing dialogs
Confirm INVITE, provisional responses, final response, and ACK evidence
Report stage boundary frames and exact observed durations

failureBranches.condition: A final non-2xx response is present
failureBranches.limitation: Report the response code as evidence without inferring operator-specific policy.

failureBranches.condition: No response or ACK is visible
failureBranches.limitation: Describe the observed signaling gap and the local completeness flag; packet loss or encrypted routing may be outside the capture.

failureBranches.condition: callSetupAnalysis requiresUserSelection is true
failureBranches.limitation: Ask the user to select a Call-ID or INVITE frame; never combine candidate dialogs.

requiredLimitations: Forked INVITEs must remain separated by Via branch.
A SIP response code alone does not establish an operator-specific root cause.
Without a correlated core-network event, do not infer a bearer or session root cause.

playbooks.title: IMS call setup delay

checks.description: Read callSetupAnalysis for exact stage durations, stage percentages, largest contribution, and boundary frames
Use only TCP/TLS evidence matched to the selected call window and endpoints; inspect other Expert evidence as uncorrelated context

successPath: Call get_communication_analysis with domains=[sip]
When the question supplies a duration such as 8 seconds, send targetSetupMillis=8000
Optionally send the playbook-configured attentionThresholdMillis only to flag stages worth reviewing
Report exact stage durations and percentages, then name the largest contribution with its frames
Treat an attention threshold as a review signal, not a universal root-cause timer

failureBranches.condition: Transaction correlation is weak or fields are missing
failureBranches.limitation: Report the timing as low-confidence and name the missing correlation fields.

failureBranches.condition: callSetupAnalysis requiresUserSelection is true
failureBranches.limitation: Ask the user to select a Call-ID or INVITE frame; never average or combine multiple dialogs.

requiredLimitations: Capture timestamps describe observed timing, not necessarily handset or network processing time.
Truncated signaling cannot establish the full setup duration.
A configured attention threshold marks a stage for review; it does not establish a network- or operator-specific timer root cause.
Without correlated core-network evidence, do not infer a bearer or session root cause.

playbooks.title: IMS call release

checks.description: Locate BYE or CANCEL and its final response
Review RTP and RTCP quality before the release

successPath: Confirm the release request and final response
Describe which endpoint sent the visible release
Separate normal release signaling from prior quality symptoms

failureBranches.condition: No BYE or CANCEL is visible
failureBranches.limitation: Do not label the call as normally released when the release path is outside the capture.

requiredLimitations: The visible BYE sender is not sufficient to assign user or network intent.
Media loss preceding release is correlation evidence, not proof of causality.

playbooks.title: IMS one-way audio

checks.description: Compare SDP direction, payload mappings, and offer-answer media endpoints
Read correlated SDP m-lines, expected directions, RTP confidence, and RTCP reports before classifying one-way media

successPath: Confirm compatible SDP direction and common codecs
Compare correlated RTP directions and their endpoint-match confidence
Report whether one-way behavior is SDP-expected or an observed anomaly with its coverage limit

failureBranches.condition: One or both RTP directions are absent
failureBranches.limitation: Use the media session coverage flag and endpoint-match confidence; absence may reflect a different capture point, encryption, NAT, or routing outside scope.

requiredLimitations: RTP at one observation point cannot prove endpoint playback behavior.
Do not label SDP sendonly or recvonly as a fault.
SDP media addresses and SIP identifiers are privacy-sensitive and must stay aliased in Agent output.

playbooks.title: RTP quality

checks.description: Read correlated RTP direction metrics, negotiated codec clock rate, sequence anomalies, and evidence frames
Compare local RTP sequence observations with reported-SSRC RTCP loss and jitter without discarding either

successPath: Report affected m-lines, directions, and their frame ranges
Compare RTP sequence metrics and RTCP reports
State the SDP clock-rate mapping and whether the capture supports a directional quality observation

failureBranches.condition: No RTCP is visible
failureBranches.limitation: No receiver feedback was captured; RTP-derived loss and jitter remain local observations, not proof of no loss.

requiredLimitations: Dynamic RTP payload types require SDP rtpmap clock rates before jitter or codec conclusions.
RTCP and local RTP sequence metrics can disagree and must both be reported.
Capture loss and endpoint media quality are distinct phenomena.

playbooks.title: Mobile core registration

checks.description: Read coreProcedures to locate the cross-protocol registration, attach, or PDU-session timeline and its local correlation ID
Locate the failed procedure stage, explicit cause, Diameter result, or experimental result and cite its frames
Check authentication and security-mode stages before assigning a registration or session failure
Query the matching SIP/IMS time window and use the local core correlation ID as a cross-layer reference

successPath: Get the core session summary and cross-protocol procedure timeline
Locate the failed procedure stage and explicit cause or result code
Check the preceding authentication and security-mode stages
Correlate the core timeline with SIP/IMS findings only by the reported time window and local correlation ID
Declare missing interfaces, encrypted signaling, and truncation boundaries

failureBranches.condition: Core identifiers or layers are unavailable
failureBranches.limitation: State which registration layers are not visible and avoid cross-layer conclusions.

failureBranches.condition: The core source is truncated or only Weak temporal edges are available
failureBranches.limitation: Report a Partial or candidate timeline; time proximity alone cannot establish a High Confidence root cause.

failureBranches.condition: NAS, SIP, or Diameter is encrypted or outside the capture point
failureBranches.limitation: State the encryption or missing-interface boundary and do not infer success, failure, or wireless-side health.

requiredLimitations: Core session identifiers, UE identifiers, TEIDs, SEIDs, realms, node IDs, APN/DNN and IMS identities are privacy-sensitive and must be aliased.
Authentication vectors, keys, integrity data, and credential values are never available to the Agent.
A partial, encrypted, or single-interface control-plane capture cannot prove end-to-end registration state.
Weak time adjacency is a candidate relationship, not a deterministic root cause.
SIP/IMS time-window overlap is correlation evidence, not proof of a core-network cause.

playbooks.title: EPS fallback

checks.description: Query RAT, registration, service, and recovery events around the call window
Compare the candidate Radio transition with NGAP/NAS and SIP call setup stages
Check whether RTP starts after the observed access-network transition without treating overlap as causality

successPath: Query Radio events in the call time range
Read the unified timeline with source clocks and uncertainty
Compare RAT and registration transitions to core and SIP stages
Report media start and any transport anomaly as separate evidence
Keep the result as a temporal candidate unless an explicit source reference exists

failureBranches.condition: Radio data is unavailable
failureBranches.limitation: Describe the SIP/core/media path as a degraded fallback and state that the wireless-side transition cannot be assessed.

failureBranches.condition: RAT or core source is truncated or encrypted
failureBranches.limitation: Report only the visible transition candidates and do not infer a completed fallback.

requiredLimitations: Missing Radio data does not establish that the wireless side was healthy.
Time proximity between RAT, core, SIP, and RTP events is a candidate correlation, not a root cause.
Encrypted NAS/NGAP or a single capture point limits EPS fallback conclusions.
Cell identifiers and subscriber identifiers remain aliased.

playbooks.title: VoNR call setup

checks.description: Check the observed RAT, registration state, and signal observations before reviewing SIP
Read the SIP call setup stages and correlate them to the Radio/Core time window
Confirm negotiated media and actual RTP start separately from call signalling

successPath: Establish whether a supported Radio source is available
Read the unified timeline and clock uncertainty
Inspect SIP call setup and core stages
Compare signal observations with setup timing only as a candidate relationship
State capture coverage and encryption boundaries

failureBranches.condition: Radio data is unavailable
failureBranches.limitation: Use SIP, core, and media evidence only; explicitly state that VoNR radio readiness and signal quality are not observable.

failureBranches.condition: SIP or NGAP is encrypted or absent
failureBranches.limitation: Do not infer VoNR registration or call setup success from Radio snapshots alone.

requiredLimitations: No Radio evidence means no conclusion about wireless signal quality or VoNR readiness.
Signal and setup-time overlap is not proof of a radio cause.
RTP visibility depends on the capture point and encryption.
Radio and core identifiers are privacy-sensitive and remain aliased.

playbooks.title: Mobility interruption

checks.description: Locate RAT changes, cell-change candidates, out-of-service, and recovery events
Inspect core, SIP, RTP/RTCP, and transport events within both source uncertainties
Check truncation, filtered scope, and source frame coverage before making a negative statement

successPath: Query Radio events around the interruption
Use the unified timeline to show uncertainty ranges
Compare control-plane, SIP, media, and transport observations
Describe candidate relationships without assigning causality
Report recovery and post-event media state separately

failureBranches.condition: Radio data is unavailable
failureBranches.limitation: Use only visible packet-layer symptoms and state that cell/RAT mobility cannot be confirmed.

failureBranches.condition: Only temporal proximity is available
failureBranches.limitation: Label the relationship as Candidate and do not convert it into a handover root cause.

requiredLimitations: A missing Radio source cannot prove mobility did not occur or that radio was healthy.
Cell-change and RAT-change events may be candidates with source uncertainty.
A media gap or SIP retry can have non-radio causes and must remain separate evidence.
Filtered or truncated captures limit recovery and absence conclusions.

playbooks.title: Radio signal degradation

checks.description: Read signal-drop observations, metric before/after values, and confidence
Compare signal candidates with SIP, RTP/RTCP, and transport symptoms in the uncertainty window
Check source capability, sampling interval, and capture coverage before excluding causes

successPath: Report the observed signal metric change and source uncertainty
Inspect registration and data state transitions
Compare packet-layer symptoms as temporal candidates
Keep signal observation and user-perceived quality as separate claims
List missing Radio, endpoint, and encryption evidence

failureBranches.condition: Radio data is unavailable
failureBranches.limitation: Diagnose only packet-layer symptoms and state that signal degradation is not observable.

failureBranches.condition: Signal samples are sparse or uncertain
failureBranches.limitation: Report the metric change as a low-confidence candidate and do not interpolate between samples.

requiredLimitations: No Radio data means no conclusion about signal quality or wireless-side health.
Signal metric changes do not prove packet loss, call failure, or user-perceived audio impact.
Telephony snapshots may omit cell identity and detailed RRC state due to Android permissions.
Time correlation includes both source uncertainties and any manual clock offset.
